extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting to Nature Portfolio journals; institutional press offices; journalists covering journal content
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial policy for how authors, institutions and journalists should handle press communication, embargoes, and preprint/conference publicity for content submitted to or accepted by Nature Portfolio journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouragement of direct solicitation of media by authors
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions. Authors should not seek media coverage ahead of this window; see 'Communications between scientists' for how embargo applies to conference presentations and preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and conditions for author discussion with media
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted contributions may be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may receive calls/emails from the media during the embargoed access period and are encouraged to cooperate so coverage is accurate and balanced. Authors whose papers are scheduled may arrange their own publicity but must strictly adhere to the media embargo and are advised to coordinate with the journal press office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release distribution and prepublication access for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal produces and distributes press releases summarizing upcoming content to a list of registered journalists, and journalists receive access to the full text of papers about a week before publication on a password-protected website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are encouraged to read the full version of any papers they wish to cover; accompanying material (e.g., News and Views article, extra images) is provided. The content of the press release and papers is embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting of especially newsworthy papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers deemed especially newsworthy are highlighted by a brief summary on the press release for that journal, written by the editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the journal may proactively summarize work, authors should expect media contact and cooperate to ensure accurate, balanced coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors may arrange their own publicity but must coordinate and respect embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may also arrange their own publicity (for instance through their institutional press offices), but they must strictly adhere to our media embargo and are advised to coordinate their own publicity with our press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination helps ensure simultaneous, fair release of information and avoids prepublication leaks that could affect coverage or editorial handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and rationale for embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nature Portfolio journals believe that their media embargo serves scientists, authors, journalists and the public by releasing information in a way that provides fair and equal access to the media, allowing informed comment based on the complete and final version of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes help journalists obtain informed reactions from independent researchers and provide confidence that claims have undergone peer review; premature release denies journalists that confidence and removes their ability to obtain independent reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for breaking embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break our embargoes have been removed from the press-release circulation list, and we shall continue to use this sanction when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking the stated time/date embargo on press release content risks removal from future privileged access to prepublication materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for open scientific communication and preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals support open communications between researchers — including posting on recognised preprint servers, preprint commenting platforms, discussions at meetings, wikis or authors' blogs — and neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers may display drafts on established preprint servers before or during submission to Nature journals; exposure of preprints does not preempt submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on media engagement about preprints and conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to requests from the media in response to a preprint or conference presentation by providing explanation or clarification of the work or information about its context; such media coverage will not hinder editorial handling of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers approached by reporters over a preprint should make it clear the paper has not yet undergone peer review, that findings are provisional and conclusions may change. Be aware such coverage may reduce or pre-empt coverage at the time of formal publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of peer review and editorial process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to keep the details of the peer review and editorial process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose reviewer identities or confidential editorial communications; maintain confidentiality even when discussing work publicly before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for reporters covering preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: We also recommend that reporters who cover preprints clearly indicate that the study has not been peer reviewed and that the claims may change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should label preprint coverage as provisional and avoid presenting unreviewed findings as established fact.
